title: Flowcharts and pseudocode

sources.coverage: Printed pages 2–25: purpose and benefits, symbols and conventions, sequence/decision/loop structures, worked average/bonus/sum/factorial/six-score examples, pseudocode, and the algorithm/pseudocode/program distinction.
Lesson 2 of 3: flowchart purpose, symbols and rules, bonus threshold, factorial and sum loops, pre-test/post-test distinction, pseudocode, and grade-pass example.

objectives.source: PDF pp. 5–9, 11; flow.md ‘The symbols’ and ‘The rules, in one breath’
operations: interpret arrows, branch labels, and terminal conventions

objectives.source: PDF pp. 2–3; flow.md ‘Why bother drawing it?’
operations: connect a visible representation to logic checking and communication
trace an explicitly expanded six-score accumulator
trace sequential comparisons that maintain and update a largest-so-far value

objectives.source: PDF pp. 11, 17; flow.md ‘Structure 2 — Decision’ and boundary discussion
operations: reason about how a boundary operator changes a branch

objectives.source: PDF pp. 10, 12, 15; flow.md ‘Structure 3 — Loop’ and ‘Pre-test and post-test loops’
operations: trace loop initialization, updates, and exit
find factorial output and first failing test

objectives.source: PDF pp. 21–22, 25; flow.md ‘Pseudocode: the middle step’
operations: distinguish flowchart, pseudocode, and exact program syntax

objectives.source: PDF pp. 23–24; flow.md student-grade pseudocode and program example
operations: calculate a four-mark average and follow an inclusive pass threshold

visualAssets.format: SVG, provided as local assets in diagrams/ and referenced on each diagram-dependent item via stimulusAsset
visualAssets.displayRequirement: Render the referenced SVG with the stem in any learner/reviewer view. A text-only stem is incomplete for items marked [Diagram].

excluded: Questions requiring exact visual details from the PDF's six-score flowchart image beyond the readable sequence; this pilot uses a clean equivalent diagram based on PDF pp. 18–20.
Python implementation details beyond the pseudocode/program distinction and lesson examples.
Flowchart standards not taught in the two sources, including formal ISO symbol variants or complexity notation.
bloomPolicy: Bloom labels are descriptive review evidence, not quotas. Create is excluded from the single-select MCQ classification; construction prompts in the structured-response set can require Create.
